inputs.provenance: SYNTHETIC demonstration, not plant data, modelled on the plant description (thicker coil rolled to thin gauge; bands along the length at several width positions, some continuous, some short-lived, worse at thinner gauge). Same single-stand four-high aluminium mill as thin_gauge_chatter_demo, final pass 0.30 -> 0.21 mm at 12 m/s, friction 0.03 supplied (the placeholder tribology closure is shown beside it, not used), flow stress computed from a synthetic Voce law (use_computed_flow_stress true), schedule 2.2 -> 0.21 mm in six passes. The roll heat share (0.08 per roll, strip_heat_fraction 0.84) and the spray coefficient were CHOSEN so that the thermal crown lands in the 2-16 um reported for mills (model: 9.7 um). limitations: Screening result on unvalidated, uncalibrated models; no plant validation is claimed.
The score is an ordinal evidence tally (supports 3/2/1 minus contradictions 6/2/1 for strong/moderate/weak), not a probability and not a certified cause.
The chatter model is linear: it cannot predict limit-cycle amplitude, mark severity or strip break, and a forced response at an unstable operating point is formal only.
Strip spans are lumped springs (inaccurate near the span wave resonance c/(2L)).
Circular (Hitchcock) roll flattening is not valid toward foil gauges; thinner passes need supplied bite sensitivities (model_options.bite_response_override).
The bite-damping closure (fraction beta of transit time) is a declared heuristic; results without it (beta = 0) are reported alongside.
Friction is an input unless tribology.use_computed_friction is set; the friction-speed closure of bite_tribology is an unfitted placeholder whose slope, not level, is used.
Fifth-octave regeneration (backup-roll marking) is screened kinematically, not simulated in time; the antisymmetric mode frequency is an undamped lumped estimate.
Spray coverage is a geometric footprint count; the phase-1 thermal growth is a free-expansion upper bound with no axial conduction (the v2 width_model solves the roll temperature field instead).
The lengthwise physics (roll thermal stripes, shape chain, coil ridges, troughs) rests on planner-derived and memory formulas flagged in each result; no plant validation.

flow_stress.note: Equivalent strain eps = prior + (2/sqrt(3))*ln(h_ref/h); the mean flow stress of each pass is the strain average over that pass (bite_tribology.schedule_flow_stress).

friction.note: PLACEHOLDER friction closure (not fitted): with ground-roll roughness it stays near the boundary regime; read the absolute friction as a placeholder and the slope with speed (dmu/du) as the useful output. With use_computed_friction the friction is a fixed point friction -> bite -> R' -> friction (at most 5 passes, tolerance 0.0001); otherwise it is evaluated once at the contact radius of the supplied-friction bite.

gauge_trend.onset_50mm_reference_basis: 0.05 m wide top-hat stripe at 0.6675 m, height bisected
gauge_trend.reference_stripe_basis: largest steady stripe (peak 5.783e-06 m at 0.6675 m), isolated; manifest onset by scaling its own shape
gauge_trend.text: Same 5.78 um roll stripe on every pass, 1.4 mm -> 0.21 mm: with the linear exit-tension feedback the I-units are 70.7 -> 108 I-units (x1.53; rigid bound x6.67). The band is slack (MANIFEST, feedback saturated) on 6 of 6 passes, where the reported I-units (184 -> 952) rise toward the compliance-only values. The thin-gauge trend comes from the band buckling stress (proportional to thickness squared: 4.26 MPa -> 0.0904 MPa for the reported band), the saturation of the feedback once a band goes slack, and the flatness dead band (half-width 13.9 -> 0.407 I-units). The stripe height at which the band first buckles under the pass tension is 12 um -> 1.23 um for a 50 mm stripe and 2.9 um -> 2.3 um for the model stripe shape. The broad thermal stripe gives a wide band whose buckling stress is small at every gauge, so its onset is set mainly by the pass tension.

inputs_used.bite_heat_basis: computed: plastic work + interface slip dissipation of the pass (slab solid_slip_dissipation_both_interfaces_w at the Hitchcock contact radius / width)

limitations: Circumferentially averaged roll temperature; top-hat spray footprints.
Shape chain: half-space roll compliance, linear exit-tension feedback with an approximate band-wise saturation, k = 4 narrow-band buckling (from memory).
Stripe detection by differencing against a healthy-header solution; the stripe threshold is an analyst choice.
Not plant-validated.

positions.tolerance_basis: one quarter of the nozzle pitch

crown.heredity_status: NOT_SUPPLIED: gap_crown_m, entry_crown_m and heredity_coefficient are all needed

thermal_events.band_life_definition: band_life_s = event duration + time after the event ends for the stripe to fall below the manifest threshold (or the reporting threshold when it never becomes manifest)
thermal_events.growth_rate_note: Radius growth follows the radial heat integral, so right after a spray change the stripe grows at 2*alpha*factor*dq/(rho*c) whatever the radial distribution; short-lived bands arise because the stripe crosses the manifest threshold within seconds to tens of seconds and fades over about a minute after the zone returns, not because the roll skin responds fast.
thermal_events.open_discrepancy: The 20 s first-order flatness response identified on a plant (Dohmae & Okamura 2012) is faster than this model's decay; possible causes (none modelled): bite heat depending on the roll surface temperature, emulsion-level heat transfer, per-revolution effects.

thermal_steady.stripe_method: difference actual header - healthy header (same pass), thresholded directly (no polynomial de-trend)
